Alright, I've set up the project skeleton: created the `package.json` with the basic metadata and a dependency on `ws`, and added `shared.js` containing physics constants, character data, and map definitions (though MAPS is truncated in the snippet). The next logical piece is the server that will host the static client files, manage WebSocket connections, and run the authoritative game simulation. 

First, I need to think about the overall architecture. The client will be a simple HTML/Canvas app that loads `shared.js` and other assets from the `public` folder. The server must serve those static files over HTTP, so I’ll use Node's built-in `http` module combined with `fs` and `path` to resolve requests safely (prevent directory traversal). I’ll also need a MIME map for common file extensions.

Next, the server must handle WebSocket connections. I’ll import `WebSocketServer` from the `ws` package and attach it to the HTTP server so that the same port serves both HTTP and WS traffic.

Now, the core of the game: an authoritative simulation loop running at 60 Hz, broadcasting snapshots at 30 Hz. I’ll define a global `game` object to hold the current phase (`lobby`, `charselect`, `mapselect`, `battle`, `victory`), a map of player objects, the selected map, timers for countdowns and victory screens, and a tick counter. A helper `now()` will give me the current time in seconds.

I need a broadcast helper that JSON‑stringifies a message and sends it to every connected player whose socket is open. Also a `participants()` helper to filter out spectators.

The lobby state needs to be sent to all clients whenever something changes, so I’ll write `lobbyState()` to construct a compact representation of the game’s current state, and `syncState()` to broadcast it.

Host promotion is important when the current host disconnects, so `promoteHost()` will assign the first remaining player as host if none have the `host` flag.

Phase transitions: 
- `toCharSelect()` sets the phase, clears winner info, resets ready/vote flags, and syncs state.
- `toMapSelect()` similarly clears votes.
- `pickMap()` tallies votes from participants and picks the most‑voted map (or a random one if none).
- `toBattle()` sets up the battle: picks a map, starts a 3‑second countdown, spawns each participant at a spawn point (cycling through the map’s spawn list), and initializes all per‑player simulation fields (position, velocity, damage, stocks, etc.). It also broadcasts a `battleStart` message with the map and countdown end time.
- `toVictory()` records the winner, timestamps the victory start, and syncs state.
- `checkBattleEnd()` looks at alive participants and decides whether to transition to victory or back to character select.

The simulation itself needs several functions:
- `respawn(p, map)` resets a knocked‑out player after the respawn delay, giving them invulnerability.
- `koPlayer(p, map)` handles a stock loss, broadcasts a KO event, and either respawns or eliminates the player, then checks for battle end.
- `tryHit(attacker, atk, others)` performs hit detection for an active attack, applying damage, knockback, hitstun, and broadcasting a hit event.
- `simPlayer(p, dt, map, others)` is the per‑player state machine: processes input, handles attack timing, movement (ground, air, drift, fast‑fall), jumping (including double jumps), dropping through thin platforms, gravity, platform collision, blast zone checks, and animation state updates.
- `battleTick(dt)` runs `simPlayer` for each participant each tick, respecting the pre‑battle countdown.
- `snapshot()` builds a compact snapshot of all participants for the client to render.

The main loop will be a `setInterval` at 60 Hz. On each tick, I’ll increment `game.tick`, run `battleTick` if in battle, and broadcast snapshots every other tick (i.e., 30 Hz). If in victory, after 6 seconds I’ll transition back to character select.

Connection handling: on a new WS connection, assign a unique ID, wait for a `join` message, create a player object (setting host flag if first player), and send a welcome packet. If the game is already in battle, also send a `battleStart`. Then sync state.

Message handling: 
- `startSelect` from the host moves from lobby to character select.
- `pickChar` records a player's character choice.
- `ready` marks a player ready; when all participants are ready and have a character, transition to map select.
- `voteMap` records a map vote; when all have voted, transition to battle.
- `input` updates the player's input state during battle.

On socket close, remove the player, possibly promote a new host, check for battle end, and reset to lobby if no players remain, then sync state.

Finally, the server should listen on the configured port, log useful information (local URL, network URLs, tunnel hint), and print a friendly banner.
